runs.failure_point: It listed only the five series matters its scans hit and never looked at the five sibling folders of the same series.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [43] said the pattern requiring the name next to 'retail' or 'holdings' would miss other name forms; the agent broadened to any 'cascade' occurrence, but the rerun still returned five of the ten series matters, and no review named the unlisted siblings.
first_error.why: Its shell unzip-and-grep scans returned client-name hits in only five of the ten matters of one numbered series, and the agent never listed the sibling folders of that series, which its own folder count at [10]-[11] showed.

divergence: Mixed (T0 and T1 pass; T2 fails, 6/11). The runs split at the first store-wide text scan. T0 and T1 used Python extraction scripts with name variants and the abbreviation, and the exact-name filter landed on all ten matters of one numbered series; they listed and read an engagement letter for each and excluded the look-alike entities. T2's scans were shell unzip/grep pipelines run in the background. The first pattern required the name next to 'retail' or 'holdings'; the review flagged that it would miss other name forms. The broadened rerun still returned only five of the ten series matters. T2 never listed the sibling folders of that series, although its own folder count showed them, and answered with five (search-miss). The critic's review at the split named the narrow pattern but not the missing siblings; later reviews flagged hand-picked candidates by naming other surfaced matters. T2's agent-defined stages (two reopened scans declared as new, hit verification, listing of other surfaced matters, an identifier check) did not recover the missing matters.
